previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for recurrent nausea and vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and insulin therapy. Her elevated blood glucose and anion gap indicated diabetic ketoacidosis, which improved with hydration, though urinary ketones remained elevated. Hypertension and tachycardia, likely due to dehydration and vomiting, resolved with fluids and resumption of oral antihypertensives. She began tolerating small amounts of food but chose to leave against medical advice before completing monitoring for DKA risk. She was discharged with an updated insulin sliding scale, instructions to pre-treat meals with anti-nausea medications, and follow-up plans with GI and psychiatry.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Nausea and vomiting: Mrs. ___ was admitted with nausea and 
vomitting.  She was afebrile with no leukocytosis.  Symptoms 
were consistent with previous episodes of gastroparesis.  She 
was treated symptommatically with IVF and anti-emetics.  
Domperidone is non-formulary at ___ and patient was unable to 
have it brought in, so she was placed on Reglan TID.  Due to 
repetitive admissions, sent urine for porphyria test, which was 
negative.  Due to concurrent hypertension with symptoms, plasma 
metanephrines were sent (pending on discharge) to eval for pheo, 
however patient was non-compliant with 24 urine collection for 
metanephrines.  On day prior to discharge, she was able to 
tolerate a saltine, but experienced continued nausea/emesis a 
few hours later.  On day of discharge, she was able to advance 
her diet to a full meal with no nausea/vomitting.  She was 
dishcarged home on outpatient medications to follow-up with her 
GI physician at previously scheduled appointment.

# DM, type 1: Glargine and humalog insulin sliding scale were 
conitnued during admission.  UA with ketones, so patient was 
placed on D5W to ensure insulin was administered.  Blood sugar 
was better controlled with further titration of HISS.  Patient 
was discharged on home dose glargine and HISS to follow-up with 
___.

# HTN: Due to inability to tolerate PO, patient was treated with 
Metoprolol IV to manage hypertension, titrated prn.  Discharged 
on home metoprolol and lisinopril.
